title: The Progress Practice

header.html: Explain the purpose of the progress practice and its relationships with the principles; explain the purpose of the checkpoint, highlight, end stage, end project, lessons and exception reports, the daily log, the lessons log and the digital and data management approach; define forecast, exception, tolerance and event-driven and time-driven controls; describe tolerances, types of control, reviewing and reporting progress and lessons, forecasting, escalating and the use of data and systems
the official PRINCE2 7 Foundation syllabus (PeopleCert), learning outcome 4.7

html:
1Purpose

The progress practice sets up mechanisms to monitor and compare actual achievements with those planned, to forecast the project's objectives and continued viability, and to control unacceptable deviations.

2Key concepts

Term Meaning
Forecast A prediction of future performance or results
Tolerance The permissible deviation above and below a plan's target before escalation is needed
Exception A situation where a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded
Event-driven control Control that happens when something occurs (end of a stage, an exception)
Time-driven control Control that happens at regular intervals (a weekly or monthly report)

Tolerance levels and escalation

Level Who sets tolerance Escalate to
Project Corporate or programme management (to the project board) Corporate or programme
Stage Project board (to the project manager) Project board
Work package Project manager (to the team manager) Project manager
Exam tip

. If a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded, it is an exception: escalate to the next level up. The board is told through an exception report.

3Reports and records

Management product From to Type Purpose
Checkpoint report team manager to project manager time-driven Progress of a work package
Highlight report project manager to board time-driven Stage progress at regular intervals
End stage report project manager to board event-driven Stage results and a view of the next
End project report project manager to board event-driven Review of the whole project at closure
Lessons report project manager event-driven Lessons for use by others
Exception report project manager to board event-driven Describes an exception, options and a recommendation
Daily log (project log) project manager ongoing Informal notes and items not captured elsewhere
Lessons log (project log) project manager ongoing All useful lessons as they appear
Digital and data management approach (PID) project manager at initiation How data and digital tools are used and protected
Exam tip

. Checkpoint = team to project manager. Highlight = project manager to board, at intervals. End stage and exception reports are event-driven.

4Progress guidance

Guidance Meaning
Tolerances for progress control Set tolerances for time, cost, quality, scope, benefits, risk, sustainability at each level
Types of control Time-driven and event-driven controls, at the board and project manager levels
Reviewing progress and lessons Compare actual with plan; learn as you go
Reporting progress and lessons Communicate status to the right people at the right time
Forecasting Predict outcomes so action is early
Escalating Raise an exception to the next level promptly
Use of data and systems Digital tools and data to track and report progress
Exam tip

. A tolerance is the allowed deviation; an exception is when it is forecast to be exceeded. Escalate as soon as it is forecast, not after it happens.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A team manager reports progress on a work package to the project manager every week. Which report is this?

  • AHighlight report
  • BCheckpoint report
  • CEnd stage report
  • DException report
Show the answer

Answer: B. A checkpoint report goes from a team manager to the project manager.

S2Which statements are CORRECT? (1) A highlight report goes from the project manager to the board. (2) An exception report is event-driven. (3) A checkpoint report goes from the board to the project manager. (4) An end stage report is time-driven.

  • A3 and 4
  • B2 and 3
  • C1 and 4
  • D1 and 2
Show the answer

Answer: D. Highlight goes to the board, and an exception report is event-driven.

S3Identify the missing word. An [ ? ] occurs when a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded.

  • AException
  • BBaseline
  • COutput
  • DOutcome
Show the answer

Answer: A. That is an exception.

S4Which control happens at regular intervals?

  • ATime-driven
  • BEvent-driven
  • CException-driven
  • DStage-driven
Show the answer

Answer: A. Time-driven controls happen at regular intervals.

S5The project manager forecasts a stage will exceed its cost tolerance. What should happen?

  • ARaise an exception to the project board
  • BHide it until the end stage report
  • CIncrease the tolerance without asking
  • DIgnore it
Show the answer

Answer: A. Escalate the exception to the board.

S6Where are useful lessons recorded as they come up?

  • AThe product register
  • BThe lessons log
  • CThe business case
  • DThe risk register
Show the answer

Answer: B. The lessons log collects lessons throughout.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Define a tolerance.

Show the answer

The permissible deviation above and below a plan's target before escalation is needed.

R2What is an exception?

Show the answer

A situation where a tolerance is forecast to be exceeded.

R3Who produces the highlight report and who receives it?

Show the answer

The project manager produces it for the project board.

R4Name two event-driven reports.

Show the answer

The end stage report and the exception report.

R5What does the daily log hold?

Show the answer

Informal notes and items not captured in other products.

R6Which product describes how data and digital tools are used and protected?

Show the answer

The digital and data management approach.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Tolerance / exception permitted deviation / tolerance forecast to be exceeded
Controls time-driven (regular) and event-driven
Reports checkpoint, highlight, end stage, end project, lessons, exception
Logs daily log and lessons log (project log)
Escalation to the next level up
